<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(Unaudited) </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">1.&#160;&#160; <span style="text-decoration:underline;">Basis of Presentation</span> </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The accompanying unaudited consolidated financial statements of Schlumberger Limited and its subsidiaries (&#8220;Schlumberger&#8221;) have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America for interim financial information and with the instructions to Form 10-Q and Article 10 of Regulation S-X.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, they do not include all of the information and footnotes required by generally accepted accounting principles for complete financial statements.&#160;&#160;In the opinion of Schlumberger management, all adjustments considered necessary for a fair statement have been included in the accompanying unaudited financial statements.&#160;&#160;All intercompany transactions and balances have been eliminated in consolidation.&#160;&#160;Operating results for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2020 are not necessarily indicative of the results that may be expected for the full year ending December&#160;31, 2020.&#160;&#160;The December&#160;31, 2019 balance sheet information has been derived from the Schlumberger 2019 audited financial statements.&#160;&#160;For further information, refer to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements</span> and notes thereto included in the Schlumberger Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December&#160;31, 2019, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on January&#160;22, 2020. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On August 31, 2020, Schlumberger and Liberty Oilfield Services Inc. (&#8220;Liberty&#8221;) entered into an agreement for the contribution to Liberty of OneStim<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>,<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top"> </sup>Schlumberger&#8217;s onshore hydraulic fracturing business in the United States and Canada, including its pressure pumping, pumpdown perforating, and Permian frac sand businesses, in exchange for a <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000472" name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentOwnershipPercentage" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapCapitalizedCostsOfUnprovedPropertiesExcludedFromAmortizationByPropertyOrProjectAxis_slbOneStimMember_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_us-gaapSalesRevenueNetMember_us-gaapTypeOfArrangementAxis_slbSchlumbergerAndLibertyOilfieldServicesIncAgreementMember_20200831" decimals="2" scale="-2">37</ix:nonFraction>% equity interest in Liberty.&#160;&#160;The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2020 and is subject to Liberty stockholder approval and other customary closing conditions.&#160;&#160;OneStim represented approximately <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000473" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapCapitalizedCostsOfUnprovedPropertiesExcludedFromAmortizationByPropertyOrProjectAxis_slbOneStimMember_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_us-gaapSalesRevenueNetMember_us-gaapTypeOfArrangementAxis_slbSchlumbergerAndLibertyOilfieldServicesIncAgreementMember_20200101_20200930" decimals="2" scale="-2">5</ix:nonFraction>% of Schlumberger&#8217;s consolidated revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2020.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000444" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200930" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000444_dcnt_165437fb-56a5-4620-832b-65db1d13e19a">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000444_dcnt_165437fb-56a5-4620-832b-65db1d13e19a" continuedAt="F_000444_dcnt_afd57cca-9ac5-4f1e-887d-01caa8e5fd8d">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">First quarter 2020:</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">Geopolitical events that increased the supply of low-priced oil to the global market occurred at the same time that demand weakened due to the worldwide effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a collapse in oil prices during March 2020.&#160;&#160;As a result, Schlumberger&#8217;s market capitalization deteriorated significantly compared to the end of 2019.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s stock price reached a low during the first quarter of 2020 not seen since 1995.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Philadelphia Oil Services Sector index, which is comprised of companies involved in the oil services sector, reached an all-time low.&#160;&#160;As a result of these facts, Schlumberger determined that it was more likely than not that the fair value of certain of its reporting units were less than their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Therefore, Schlumberger performed an interim goodwill impairment test.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000534" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF">11</ix:nonFraction> reporting units with goodwill balances aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000535" name="us-gaap:GoodwillGross" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">16.0</ix:nonFraction> billion.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger determined that the fair value of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000536" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbFourReportingUnitsMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">four</ix:nonFraction> of its reporting units, representing $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000537" name="us-gaap:GoodwillGross" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbFourReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">4.5</ix:nonFraction> billion of the goodwill, was substantially in excess of their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger performed a detailed quantitative impairment assessment of the remaining <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000538" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSevenReportingUnitsMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">seven</ix:nonFraction> reporting units, which represented $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000539" name="us-gaap:GoodwillGross" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSevenReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">11.5</ix:nonFraction> billion of goodwill. As a result of this assessment, Schlumberger concluded that the goodwill associated with each of these seven reporting units was impaired, resulting in a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000540" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetImpairment" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">3.1</ix:nonFraction> billion goodwill impairment charge.&#160;&#160;This charge primarily relates to goodwill associated with the Drilling and Production segments.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Following the $3.1 billion goodwill impairment charge relating to these seven reporting units, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000541" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">six</ix:nonFraction> of these reporting units had a remaining goodwill balance.&#160;&#160;These six reporting units had goodwill balances which ranged between $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000542" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.2</ix:nonFraction> billion and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000543" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">5.0</ix:nonFraction> billion and aggregated to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000544" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSixReportingUnitsMember_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">8.4</ix:nonFraction> billion as of March 31, 2020. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger used the income approach to estimate the fair value of its reporting units, but also considered the market approach to validate the results.&#160;&#160;The income approach estimates the fair value by discounting each reporting unit&#8217;s estimated future cash flows using Schlumberger&#8217;s estimate of the discount rate, or expected return, that a marketplace participant would have required as of the valuation date.&#160;&#160;The market approach includes the use of comparative multiples to corroborate the discounted cash flow results. The market approach involves significant judgement involved in the selection of the appropriate peer group companies and valuation multiples.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the income approach include the estimated future net annual cash flows for each reporting unit and the discount rate.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger selected the assumptions used in the discounted cash flow projections using historical data supplemented by current and anticipated market conditions and estimated growth rates.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s estimates are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable.&#160;&#160;However, given the inherent uncertainty in determining the assumptions underlying a discounted cash flow analysis, particularly in the current volatile market, actual results may differ from those used in Schlumberger&#8217;s valuations which could result in additional impairment charges in the future.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The discount rates utilized to value Schlumberger&#8217;s reporting units were between <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000545" name="slb:DiscountRateUtilized" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="3" scale="-2">12.0</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000546" name="slb:DiscountRateUtilized" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="3" scale="-2">13.5</ix:nonFraction>%, depending on the risks and uncertainty inherent in the respective reporting unit as well as the size of the reporting unit.&#160;&#160;Assuming all other assumptions and inputs used in each of the respective discounted cash flow analysis were held constant, a <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000547" name="slb:ExpectedIncreaseDecreaseInDiscountRateAssumption" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="4" scale="-4">50</ix:nonFraction>-basis point increase or decrease in the discount rate assumptions would have changed the fair value of the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000548" name="slb:NumberOfReportingUnitsFairValueToBeImpacted" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">seven</ix:nonFraction> reporting units, on average, by less than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000549" name="slb:ExpectedPercentageChangeInFairValueOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="2" scale="-2">5</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">During August 2019, Schlumberger&#8217;s market capitalization deteriorated significantly compared to the end of the second quarter of 2019.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s stock price reached a low not seen since 2005.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Philadelphia Oil Services Sector Index, which is comprised of companies involved in the oil services sector, reached an 18-year low.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a result of these facts, Schlumberger determined that it was more likely than not that the fair value of certain of its reporting units were less than their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Therefore, Schlumberger performed an interim goodwill impairment test as of August 31, 2019.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of August 31, 2019, Schlumberger had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000599" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF">17</ix:nonFraction> reporting units with goodwill balances aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000600" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">25.0</ix:nonFraction> billion.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger determined that the fair value of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000601" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSevenReportingUnitsMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">seven</ix:nonFraction> of its reporting units, representing approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000602" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbSevenReportingUnitsMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">13.8</ix:nonFraction> billion of the goodwill, was substantially in excess of their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger performed a detailed quantitative impairment assessment of the remaining <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000603" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbTenReportingUnitsMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF">10</ix:nonFraction> reporting units, which represented $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000604" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbTenReportingUnitsMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">11.2</ix:nonFraction> billion of goodwill. As a result of this assessment, Schlumberger concluded that the goodwill associated with <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000605" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbNineReportingUnitsMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">nine</ix:nonFraction> of the 10 reporting units was impaired, resulting in an $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000606" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetImpairment" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbNineReportingUnitsMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">8.8</ix:nonFraction> billion goodwill impairment charge.&#160;&#160;This charge primarily relates to Schlumberger&#8217;s Drilling and Cameron segments.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Following the $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000608" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetImpairment" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbNineReportingUnitsMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">8.8</ix:nonFraction> billion goodwill impairment charge relating to these <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000607" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbNineReportingUnitsMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">nine</ix:nonFraction> reporting units, only <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000609" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbThreeReportingUnitsMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">three</ix:nonFraction> had a remaining goodwill balance.&#160;&#160;These three reporting units had goodwill balances which ranged between $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000610" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbThreeReportingUnitsMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.4</ix:nonFraction> billion and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000611" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbThreeReportingUnitsMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.6</ix:nonFraction> billion and aggregated to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000612" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbThreeReportingUnitsMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">1.5</ix:nonFraction> billion as of August 31, 2019. The <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000613" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbReportingUnitOneMember_20190831_20190831" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">ten</ix:nonFraction>th reporting unit, which was determined not to be impaired, had $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000614" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapReportingUnitAxis_slbReportingUnitOneMember_20190831" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.9</ix:nonFraction> billion of goodwill.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger primarily used the income approach to estimate the fair value of its reporting units, but also considered the market approach to validate the results.&#160;&#160;The income approach estimates the fair value by discounting each reporting unit&#8217;s estimated future cash flows using Schlumberger&#8217;s estimate of the discount rate, or expected return, that a marketplace participant would have required as of the valuation date.&#160;&#160;The market approach includes the use of comparative multiples to corroborate the discounted cash flow results.&#160;&#160;The market approach involves significant judgement involved in the selection of the appropriate peer group companies and valuation multiples.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the income approach include the estimated future net annual cash flows for each reporting unit and the discount rate.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger selected the assumptions used in the discounted cash flow projections using historical data supplemented by current and anticipated market conditions and estimated growth rates.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s estimates are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable.&#160;&#160;However, given the inherent uncertainty in determining the assumptions underlying a discounted cash flow analysis, actual results may differ from those used in Schlumberger&#8217;s valuations which could result in additional impairment charges in the future.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The discount rates utilized to value Schlumberger&#8217;s reporting units were between <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000615" name="slb:DiscountRateUtilized" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20190701_20190930" decimals="3" scale="-2">12.5</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000616" name="slb:DiscountRateUtilized" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190701_20190930" decimals="3" scale="-2">14.0</ix:nonFraction>%, depending on the risks and uncertainty inherent in the respective reporting unit.&#160;&#160;Assuming all other assumptions and inputs used in each of the respective discounted cash flow analysis were held constant, a <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000617" name="slb:ExpectedIncreaseInDiscountRateAssumption" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190701_20190930" decimals="4" scale="-4">50</ix:nonFraction> basis point increase in the discount rate assumption would have increased the goodwill impairment charge by approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000618" name="slb:IncreaseInGoodwillImpairmentCharge" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190701_20190930" decimals="-8" <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000619" name="slb:ExpectedDecreaseInDiscountRateAssumption" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190701_20190930" decimals="4" scale="-4">50</ix:nonFraction> basis point decrease in the discount rate assumption would have decreased the goodwill impairment charge by approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000620" name="slb:DecreaseInGoodwillImpairmentCharge" contextRef="C_0000087347_20190701_20190930" decimals="-8" scale="9">0.4</ix:nonFraction> billion.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10.&#160;&#160; <span style="text-decoration:underline;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</span> </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to market risks related to fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates.&#160; To mitigate these risks, Schlumberger utilizes derivative instruments.&#160; Schlumberger does not enter into derivative transactions for speculative purposes. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest Rate Risk </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is subject to interest rate risk on its debt and its investment portfolio.&#160; Schlumberger maintains an interest rate risk management strategy that uses a mix of variable and fixed rate debt combined with its investment portfolio, to mitigate the exposure to changes in interest rates.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At September 30, 2020, Schlumberger had fixed rate debt aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000967" name="slb:FixedRateDebt" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200930" decimals="-8" scale="9">16.6</ix:nonFraction> billion and variable rate debt aggregating $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000968" name="slb:VariableRateDebt" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200930" decimals="-8" scale="9">1.2</ix:nonFraction> billion. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Foreign Currency Exchange Rate Risk </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a multinational company, Schlumberger generates revenue in more than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbCountry" id="F_000969" name="us-gaap:NumberOfCountriesInWhichEntityOperates" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200930" decimals="INF">120</ix:nonFraction> countries. Schlumberger&#8217;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar.&#160; However, outside the United States, a significant portion of Schlumberger&#8217;s expenses are incurred in foreign currencies.&#160; Therefore, when the US dollar weakens (strengthens) in relation to the foreign currencies of the countries in which Schlumberger conducts business, the US dollar-reported expenses will increase (decrease).&#160;&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency.&#160; Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks.&#160; These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in the fair value of the hedge recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet </span>and in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss.&#160; </span>Amounts recorded in<span style="font-style:italic;"> Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss </span>are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&#160; </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">18</p>

Schlumberger uses cross-currency swaps to provide a hedge against these cash flow risks. </span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to changes in the fair value of assets and liabilities that are denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160; While Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts and foreign currency options to economically hedge this exposure as it relates to certain currencies, these contracts are not designated as hedges for accounting purposes.&#160; Instead, the fair value of the contracts is recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet, </span>and changes in the fair value are recognized in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Loss </span>as are changes in fair value of the hedged item.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At September 30, 2020, contracts were outstanding for the US dollar equivalent of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001022" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapForeignExchangeContractMember_20200930" decimals="INF" scale="9">10.9</ix:nonFraction> billion in various foreign currencies, of which $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001023" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapForeignExchangeContractMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_us-gaapDebtMember_us-gaapHedgingDesignationAxis_us-gaapDesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_20200930" decimals="INF" scale="9">6.7</ix:nonFraction> billion relates to hedges of debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At September 30, 2020, Schlumberger recognized a cumulative $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001024" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyCashFlowHedgeGainLossReclassifiedToEarningsNet" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200930" decimals="-6" scale="6">218</ix:nonFraction> million loss in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss</span> relating to changes in the fair value of foreign currency forward contracts and cross-currency swaps.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Due to the actions taken by Schlumberger to reduce its global workforce during 2020, Schlumberger experienced a significant reduction in the expected aggregate years of future service of its employees in its US postretirement medical plan. Accordingly, Schlumberger recorded a curtailment gain of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001307" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanRecognizedNetGainLossDueToSettlementsAndCurtailments1" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_slbImpairmentAndOtherMember_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_us-gaapDefinedBenefitPostretirementHealthCoverageMember_20200401_20200630" decimals="-6" scale="6">69</ix:nonFraction> million during the second quarter of 2020 relating to this plan. The curtailment gain includes recognition of the decrease in the benefit obligation as well as a portion of the previously unrecognized prior service credit, reflecting the reduction in expected years of future service.&#160; As a result of the curtailment, Schlumberger performed a remeasurement of the plan, which had an immaterial impact.&#160; This gain was classified in <span style="font-style:italic;">Impairments &#38; other</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Loss</span>.&#160; See Note 2 &#8211; <span style="font-style:italic;">Charges and Credits</span>.</p>

<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Charges and credits are described in detail in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter 2020 revenue declined 2% sequentially, as North America revenue was 2% lower and international revenue declined 1%. In North America land, increased completions activity on drilled but uncompleted (&#8220;DUC&#8221;) wells was offset by reduced drilling in US land. North America offshore was affected by reduced rig activity, lower multiclient seismic license sales, and hurricane disruption.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">International revenue was driven by higher activity in Latin America, boosted by the resumption of production in the Asset Performance Solutions (&#8220;APS&#8221;) projects in Ecuador and increased seasonal summer activity in the North Sea and Russia. These increases were offset by the effects of rig count declines and extended COVID-19 disruptions in Africa and in the Middle East &#38; Asia.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Looking to the fourth quarter of 2020, Schlumberger expects to continue to benefit from the effectiveness of its strategy, disciplined approach to North America, and broad strength of its international business, as reflected in the third-quarter results. In North America, the conditions are set for continued momentum, with improving DUC well completion activity in US land and a modest drilling resumption in the US and Canada. International activity is steady following the budget resets completed in the third quarter and activity will be affected by the seasonal decline in the Northern Hemisphere, partly offset by muted year-end product and multiclient license sales.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Overall internationally, Schlumberger views the next two quarters as a period of transition for our industry at the trough of this cycle. Improving demand recovery supported by various government measures to stimulate economic activity and continued supply discipline from the major producers set the conditions for a long-term activity rebound. However, while the global lockdowns are evolving and vaccine development is progressing, the near-term recovery remains fragile owing to potential subsequent waves of COVID-19 that could pose a significant risk to this outlook.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On August 31, 2020, Schlumberger and Liberty Oilfield Services Inc. (&#8220;Liberty&#8221;) entered into an agreement for the contribution to Liberty of OneStim<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>,<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top"> </sup>Schlumberger&#8217;s onshore hydraulic fracturing business in the United Stated and Canada, including its pressure pumping, pumpdown perforating, and Permian frac sand businesses, in exchange for a 37% equity interest in Liberty.&#160;&#160;The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2020 and is subject to Liberty stockholder approval and other customary closing conditions.&#160;&#160;OneStim represented approximately 5% of Schlumberger&#8217;s consolidated revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2020.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">24</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization revenue of $1.0 billion decreased 4% sequentially. North America and international revenues declined 14% and 2%, respectively. This was mainly due to lower WesternGeco<span style="color:#000000;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></span> multiclient seismic license sales in North America offshore. Revenue was also lower in the Middle East due to reduced WesternGeco activity as a result of a completed project and lower Testing Services activity due to project cancellations and delays. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization pretax operating margin of 17% contracted 90 basis points (&#8220;bps&#8221;) sequentially due to lower sales of WesternGeco multiclient seismic licenses, which impacted North America margin, while international margin was flat sequentially.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling revenue of $1.5 billion decreased 12% sequentially. North America and international revenues declined 16% and 11%, respectively. The revenue decline in North America was primarily due to lower activity in US land as rig count dropped 29%, along with rig count reductions and activity disruptions in the US Gulf of Mexico due to a more active hurricane season. In addition, extended COVID-19 disruptions caused drilling activities to be suspended or deferred in several international GeoMarkets. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling pretax operating margin of 10% was essentially flat sequentially, despite the significant revenue decline. Margin was resilient both in North America and internationally supported by prompt cost reduction measures.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production revenue of $1.8 billion increased 12% sequentially. North America and international revenues increased 13% and 11%, respectively. This was driven primarily by the gradual recovery in DUC well completions activity in US land and the resumption of APS production in Ecuador following a major landslide that led to the rupture of the main pipeline last quarter. OneStim revenue grew more than 50% sequentially as US-market stage counts increased by more than 30%.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production pretax operating margin of 13% expanded by 11 percentage points sequentially. The margin expansion was due to the resumption of production in APS projects in Ecuador and improved profitability across each of Completions, Artificial Lift Solutions, and Well Services, supported by cost reduction measures. OneStim margin improved due to better operating leverage as revenue increased by more than 50%. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron revenue of $965 million decreased 5% sequentially primarily due to declines in the long-cycle businesses of OneSubsea<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> and Drilling Systems, driven by projects ending in Asia and Europe, coupled with the extended COVID-19 disruptions. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron pretax operating margin of 6% declined by 162 bps sequentially. The margin contraction was primarily due to the unfavorable mix where contribution from the long-cycle businesses of OneSubsea and Drilling Systems was lower due to reduced activity. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:5pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:5pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">25</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Third</span><span style="text-decoration:underline;"> Quarter 20</span><span style="text-decoration:underline;">20</span><span style="text-decoration:underline;"> Compared to </span><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Third</span><span style="text-decoration:underline;"> </span><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Quarter 20</span><span style="text-decoration:underline;">19</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Interest expense excludes amounts which are included in the segments&#8217; income ($7 million in 2020&#59; $9 million in 2019).</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(4)</sup></span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Charges and credits are described in detail in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter 2020 revenue of $5.3 billion was 38% lower compared to the same period last year due to the significant fall in North America activity while international activity dropped due to downward revisions to customer budgets accentuated by COVID-19 disruptions. North America revenue declined 59% reflecting the continued capital discipline of North America operators, who reduced drilling and frac activity. International revenue decreased 27% due to COVID-19-related disruptions, the drop in offshore activity, and reduced customer discretionary spending.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter 2020 revenue of $1.0 billion decreased 39% year-on-year mainly due to lower Wireline and WesternGeco revenues as customers reduced activity due to COVID-19 and cut discretionary spending and exploration in several international GeoMarkets.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 512 bps to 17% largely due to the revenue declines in Wireline and WesternGeco.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter <span style="color:#auto;">2020 revenue of $1.5 billion </span>decreased 39% year-on-year primarily due to the activity decline in US land as rig count dropped significantly, while COVID-19 disruptions caused drilling activities to be cancelled or suspended in several international GeoMarkets. Revenue was also lower due to the divestiture of the Drilling Tools businesses at the end of the fourth quarter of 2019.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 292 bps to 10% primarily due to the significant reduction in activity in North America. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter <span style="color:#auto;">2020 revenue of $1.8 billion </span>decreased 43% year-on-year. This revenue decrease was driven by the sharp drop in OneStim pressure pumping activity in North America land<span style="color:#auto;"> as customers exercised capital discipline and revised budgets downward. Internationally, revenue was affected by COVID-19-related disruptions and reduced customer spending.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">26</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin increased 347 bps to 13% despite the significant drop in revenue. Margin improvement was supported by cost reduction measures and reduced depreciation and amortization following the asset impairment charges relating to OneStim and APS that were recorded in the second quarter of 2020.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter 2020 revenue of $1.0 billion decreased 29% year-on-year primarily as a result of lower Valves &#38; Process Systems and Surface Systems revenues in North America. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 644 bps to 6% due to reduced Surface Systems and Valves &#38; Process Systems profitability in North America and lower OneSubsea margins internationally.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Nine Months 2020 Compared to Nine Months 2019</span></p>

<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(4)</sup></span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Charges and credits are described in detail in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2020 revenue of $18.1 billion was 27% lower compared to the same period last year due to the significant fall in North America activity, as well as the international activity drop due to downward revisions to customer budgets accentuated by COVID-19 disruptions. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">North America revenue declined 45%, reflecting the continued capital discipline of North America operators, who reduced drilling and frac activity.&#160;&#160;International revenue decreased 17%.&#160;&#160;The decline was most prominent in Latin America, Europe, and Africa due to COVID-19-related restrictions, the drop in offshore activity, and the effect of the APS production interruption in Ecuador during the second quarter of 2020. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Characterization </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2020 revenue of $3.4 billion decreased 28% year-on-year primarily due to lower Wireline and WesternGeco revenue as customers reduced activity due to COVID-19 and cut discretionary spending and exploration in several international GeoMarkets. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 459 bps to 16% due to reduced profitability largely in Wireline and WesternGeco.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">27</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Drilling </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month <span style="color:#auto;">2020 revenue of $5.5 billion </span>decreased 24% year-on-year due to the activity decline in US land as rig count decreased significantly, while COVID-19 disruptions caused drilling activities to be cancelled or suspended in several international GeoMarkets. Revenue was also lower due to the divestiture of the Drilling Tools businesses at the end of the fourth quarter of 2019.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 184 bps to 11% primarily due to the decrease in revenue and COVID-19-related disruptions.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month <span style="color:#auto;">2020 revenue of $6.1 billion </span>decreased 33% year-on-year. This revenue decrease was primarily driven by the sharp drop in OneStim <span style="color:#auto;">pressure-pumping activity in North America land, lower APS revenue due to the significant production interruption in Ecuador during the second quarter of 2020 and COVID-19-related disruptions.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin was essentially flat at 8% despite the significant drop in revenue. The margin was resilient as it was supported by cost reduction measures as well as reduced depreciation and amortization following the asset impairment charges relating to OneStim and APS that were recorded in the second quarter of 2020.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cameron </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2020 revenue of $3.2 billion decreased 18% year-on-year driven by lower Valves &#38; Process Systems and Surface Systems revenue in North America. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin decreased 421 bps to 8% due to the revenue decline.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Interest and Other Income</span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2020 was (35)%, as compared to 5% for the same period of 2019.&#160; The charges described in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements</span> reduced the effective tax rate by 55 and 11 percentage points for the third quarter of 2020 and 2019, respectively, as a significant portion of these charges were not tax-effective.&#160; Changes in the geographic mix of pretax earnings accounted for the remaining increase in the effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2020 as compared to the same period of 2019.&#160;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The first quarter 2020 results did not include any benefit from reduced depreciation and amortization expense as a result of the first quarter impairment charges.&#160; However, commencing with the second quarter of 2020, depreciation and amortization expense was reduced by approximately $95 million on a quarterly basis as a result of the first quarter impairment charges.&#160;&#160;Approximately $45 million of this quarterly reduction is reflected in the Production segment, with the remaining $50 million reflected in the &#8220;Corporate &#38; other&#8221; line item. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The second quarter 2020 results did not include any benefit from reduced expenses associated with the second quarter restructuring and impairment charges. However, commencing with the third quarter of 2020, depreciation and amortization expense was reduced by approximately $80 million and lease expense was reduced by $25 million, on a quarterly basis.&#160;&#160;Approximately $70 million of this quarterly reduction is reflected in the Production Segment, with the remaining $35 million reflected amongst the Reservoir Characterization, Drilling and Cameron segments.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The third quarter 2020 results did not include any benefit from reduced expenses associated with the third quarter restructuring charges. However, going forward depreciation and&#160;lease expense will be reduced by $15 million, on a quarterly basis. This quarterly reduction will be reflected amongst all of the segments.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As these impairment charges were effective as of August 31, 2019, the third quarter 2019 results include a one-month reduction in depreciation and amortization expense of $27 million.&#160;&#160;Approximately $21 million of this amount relates to the Production segment.&#160;&#160;The remaining $6 million is reflected in the &#8220;Corporate &#38; other&#8221; line item.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no charges or credits recorded during the first six months of 2019.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As market conditions evolve and Schlumberger continues to develop its strategy to deal with such conditions, it may result in further restructuring and/or impairment charges in future periods.<span style="color:#000000;font-family:Segoe UI;"> </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The <span style="color:#000000;">effects of the COVID-19 pandemic have resulted in a significant and swift reduction in international and U.S. economic activity. These effects have adversely affected the demand for oil and natural gas, as well as for Schlumberger&#8217;s products and services, and </span>caused significant volatility and disruption of the financial markets. This period of extreme economic disruption, low oil prices and reduced demand for Schlumberger&#8217;s products and services has had, and is likely to continue to have, a material adverse impact on Schlumberger&#8217;s business, results of operations, financial condition and, at times, access to sources of liquidity. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In view of the uncertainty of the depth and extent of the contraction in oil demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic combined with the weaker commodity price environment, Schlumberger has turned its strategic focus to cash conservation and protecting its balance sheet. As a result, in April 2020 Schlumberger announced a 75% reduction to its quarterly cash dividend. The revised dividend supports Schlumberger&#8217;s value proposition through a balanced approach of shareholder distributions and organic investment, while providing the flexibility to weather the uncertain environment. This decision reflects the Company&#8217;s focus on its capital stewardship program as well as its commitment to maintain both a strong liquidity position and a strong investment grade credit rating that provides privileged access to the financial markets.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Details of the components of liquidity as well as changes in liquidity follow:<span style="font-size:12pt;">&#160;</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk affecting Schlumberger, see Item&#160;7A, &#8220;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk,&#8221; of the Schlumberger Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December&#160;31, 2019. Schlumberger&#8217;s exposure to market risk has not changed materially since December&#160;31, 2019.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_4_Controls_and_Procedures"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;4. Controls and Procedures. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger has carried out an evaluation under the supervision and with the participation of Schlumberger&#8217;s management, including the Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) and the Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;), of the effectiveness of Schlumberger&#8217;s &#8220;disclosure controls and procedures&#8221; (as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)) as of the end of the period covered by this report. Based on this evaluation, the CEO and the CFO have concluded that, as of the end of the period covered by this report, Schlumberger&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures were effective to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in the reports that Schlumberger files or submits under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms. Schlumberger&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures include controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to its management, including the CEO and the CFO, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. There was no change in Schlumberger&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting during the quarter to which this report relates that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, Schlumberger&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</p>

Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities and Use of Proceeds. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Issuer Repurchases of Equity Securities </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of September 30, 2020, Schlumberger had repurchased $1.0 billion of Schlumberger common stock under its $10 billion share repurchase program. Schlumberger did not repurchase any of its common stock during the third quarter of 2020. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_3_Defaults_Upon_Senior_Securities"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;3. Defaults Upon Senior Securities. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None<span style="font-weight:bold;">. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_4_Mine_Safety_Disclosures"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;4. Mine Safety Disclosures. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our mining operations are subject to regulation by the federal Mine Safety and Health Administration under the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977. Information concerning mine safety violations or other regulatory matters required by section 1503(a) of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act and Item&#160;104 of Regulation S-K is included in Exhibit 95 to this report.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_5_Other_Information"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;5. Other Information. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2013, Schlumberger completed the wind down of its service operations in Iran. Prior to this, certain non-US subsidiaries provided oilfield services to the National Iranian Oil Company and certain of its affiliates (&#8220;NIOC&#8221;).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger&#8217;s residual transactions or dealings with the government of Iran during the third quarter of 2020 consisted of payments of taxes and other typical governmental charges. Certain non-US subsidiaries of Schlumberger maintain depository accounts at the Dubai branch of Bank Saderat Iran (&#8220;Saderat&#8221;), and at Bank Tejarat (&#8220;Tejarat&#8221;) in Tehran and in Kish for the deposit by NIOC of amounts owed to non-US subsidiaries of Schlumberger for prior services rendered in Iran and for the maintenance of such amounts previously received. One non-US subsidiary also maintained an account at Tejarat for payment of local expenses such as taxes. Schlumberger anticipates that it will discontinue dealings with Saderat and Tejarat following the receipt of all amounts owed to Schlumberger for prior services rendered in Iran.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">34</p>
